Ticket T-0264: Cluster queue sync so an enqueue on either Mac shows on both within 3 seconds
R-048 One queue and one board across machines.
  - With cluster queue on MacBook and Mac mini, enqueueing ticket T on either machine shows T in `swarm queue list` on both within 3 seconds.
  - Only one machine holds an active lease on T; a second worker starting T gets exit non-zero and message `leased elsewhere`.
  - Swarm Watch queue depth for the shared project matches on both machines within 1 ticket.
Acceptance (each line has a tag; the ticket is done only when every line is met):
- AC1: With cluster queue on MacBook and Mac mini, a ticket enqueued on either machine shows in swarm queue list on both within 3 seconds.
This ticket owns no test file: do not write tests, test blocks or import.meta.vitest in your source files, and do not run the test runner. Prove your work with the type check (and lint) and by reading your code against each line. A line that needs a test belongs to the test ticket; a reviewer checks the rest against your code.
Use the dependency versions in package.json; do not assume other major versions.
Watch out for (background from past lessons; it does not change the task, the files or the outputs):
- Keep a worker's own failure reason next to the job record, and never let a later generic message stand in for a blocked envelope. [build, redaction, secrets, worker-output]
- Run a toolchain sync once, outside the sandbox, before the worker starts, and grant the narrow extra reads that a synced toolchain actually needs to find itself. [build, manifest, sandbox, worker-output]
- A feature that talks to another machine is not done until a test runs it against a real host; stub transports prove only the scheduling around it. [build, sandbox, ssh-remote, tool]
Work only on the files you own; report the ticket id.
